briefing.summary: Dive to the German battleship Bismarck, scuttled and sunk on 27 May 1941 after a three-day Royal Navy pursuit, and found by Robert Ballard's expedition on 8 June 1989. Scan the main hull, resting upright on the flank of an extinct seamount, then survey the detached gun turrets and the slope below her.
facts: This is a war grave. Roughly 2,100 of the 2,221 men aboard died; only about 114 were rescued. The game has no salvage, collection or loot of any kind.
Bismarck struck the seamount's flank, triggering a small landslide, and slid some distance down-slope before coming to rest upright and largely intact.
You start at the surface about 1.5 km north-east of the hull. Head south-west (about 225°) and descend.

This mission is set at the H.M.S. Hood Association's 2001 expedition fix (48.15N, 16.117W, 'vicinity of 4809N 01607W'), the most specific sourced coordinate found -- about 20 km south of an earlier, unsourced coordinate this pack previously used. The commonly quoted 48°10'N 16°12'W (Wikipedia's rounded infobox figure) sits about 6 km away. This tile's own terrain reads roughly 4,220 m at the hull -- shallower than the published 4,790-4,791 m wreck depth -- because this point sits higher on the seamount's flank than where the hull is reported to have finally settled; see the field guide's overview entry.
The hull is an artist's reconstruction at that coordinate. Open bathymetry here has no dedicated survey of the wreck itself and cannot show the ship or the real debris trail.
hazards: Total darkness below a few hundred metres; only your lights work.
Crushing pressure: roughly 480 atmospheres at this depth. Your Class C hull is rated well beyond it.
Steep, unstable seamount flank terrain near the wreck.
Unexploded ordnance may remain aboard. Keep a respectful distance and do not touch anything.
briefing.memorial_note: Bismarck is a war grave. Roughly 2,100 of her crew of 2,221 died when she sank on 27 May 1941. Please treat this site the way you would any grave: look and learn, but do not disturb. There is no salvage, collection or loot of any kind, here or anywhere in this game, and nothing here is framed as treasure or salvage.

objectives.title: Locate and scan the main hull
objectives.hint: The reconstructed Bismarck hull stands on the seamount's southeastern flank, around 4,210 m.

objectives.title: Survey the detached gun turrets down-slope
objectives.hint: Look for an illustrative detached-turret marker east of the hull on the seamount slope, around 4,120 m; exact turret positions are uncertain.

objectives.title: Examine the battle-damage debated by historians
objectives.hint: The illustrative battle-damage marker is close to Bismarck's main hull, around 4,210 m; it does not map individual hits.

objectives.title: Sample the real seamount slope below the wreck
objectives.hint: Survey the real seamount flank east and upslope of the hull, around 4,180 m; this is terrain, not a surveyed skid trail.

objectives.title: Pay respects at the memorial marker
objectives.hint: The memorial marker is beside the hull on the seamount flank, around 4,210 m.
